messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: gpu pool gpool-prod-3 queued_tasks=9850 (96%); autoscaler attempted scale (5 retries) -> reason=scale_gate_rate_limit
maya (oncall): whoa, big queue spike — paging. Any immediate customer impact? :rotating_light:
sam-ops: frontend reports 502s/timeouts hitting /v1/infer. p99 latency + CPU on frontend boxes. queue depth ~9.8k and rising. autoscaler returned provider 429s when calling scale API.
lia-sre: runtime logs shipped by runtime-bot show lots of CUDA/Xid errors and kernel OOMs on several GPU hosts. nodes flapping between Ready/NotReady.
runtime-bot: [log-sample]
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:10Z] cuda XID=31 ECC memory error
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] driver: GPU allocation failed, OOM allocating 1.2GB
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] kubelet: marking node-42 NotReady
```
eli-ml: XID 31 + OOM suggests driver/kernel regressions. That would make GPUs invisible intermittently and drop effective capacity — autoscaler sees nodes but they don't serve.
jordan-eng: autoscaler also hit a scale-gate: we have ramp limit 20% per 10m and provider token bucket exhausted from repeated scale attempts.
maya (oncall): immediate mitigations?
sam-ops: propose quick list:
1) emergency bypass: request forced on-demand instances from cloud account-b (we have spare quota)
2) cordon & drain the flapping nodes, migrate pods to healthy nodes
3) rollback the driver/kernel module pushed ~30m ago on suspect hosts
4) pause non-critical batch/eval jobs and throttle background workloads
I'll kick off 1 & 2 now.
lia-sre: add 5) traffic shaping: route non-enterprise traffic to a smaller quantized model to drop memory footprint.
maya (oncall): doing driver rollback on node-42/node-37/node-19 now. Running check: `redwoodctl node status --pool gpool-prod-3 | grep flapping`
sam-ops: kicked off emergency infra reserve: `infractl compute reserve --count 4 --zone us-west2-b --reason emergency` — provider accepted; provisioning started.
runtime-bot: INFO draining node-19,node-37,node-42. evicting ~150 pods; eviction slowness because of backlog.
eli-ml: starting a 30% canary split to lm-small-quant for non-Dedicated customers to reduce per-request memory: `gatewayctl route update /v1/infer --split 70:30 --variants model=lm-prod:model=lm-small-quant`. Expect lower p95 on canary path.
jordan-eng: applied autoscaler override +4 instances; also bumped ramp to 40% for 10m. watch warmup (~90s/node).
customer-success: field reports: four customers reported degraded latency; one reported >5% error rate. drafting an outbound advisory.
maya (oncall): created INC-2026-0315-09 and pinned thread. assigning pager to maya + lia-sre.
sam-ops: note — some device-plugin pods crash after driver crash; will force-delete nvidia-device-plugin pods on those nodes post-cordon to ensure kubelet sees devices after restart: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l name=nvidia-device-plugin --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-37`
lia-sre: rolling back driver patch id 20260315.rolled-back on node-37 — restarting nvidia modules.
maya (oncall): node-37 back to Ready. node-42 still NotReady, scheduling reboot in +5m.
eli-ml: canary route shows p95 drop ~28% on the small model path; total queue growth slowed to ~6.2k. good signal.
jordan-eng: autoscaler metrics: effective GPUs still ~12% below nominal because some nodes report devices but only 50% of GPUs visible due to driver issues. need runtime-agent restart on affected hosts.
sam-ops: restarted runtime-agent on node-19; GPUs reappeared in kubelet. evictions finished for node-19.
customer-success: outbound note ready. we'll state: hosted inference degraded, timeouts observed, remediation in progress, no PII/data loss.
maya (oncall): mitigation status:
- forced +4 instances requested (2/4 provisioned)
- driver rollback in progress (1/3 nodes recovered)
- runtime-agent restarts ongoing
- 30% canary to lm-small-quant active
- paused batch/eval jobs
Next: finish node recoveries, wait for queue <1k, then revert routing and lift scale override.
lia-sre: additional ops steps: cap KV cache entries for affected models to reduce memory churn: `configctl set model.lm-prod.cache_max 1000 --pool gpool-prod-3`.
eli-ml: applying cache cap now.
jordan-eng: autoscaler logs show last failures: provider 429 then scale_gate rejection because spot-churn risk >0.6. toggled spot-avoid to prefer on-demand for emergency override.
sam-ops: infra update: all 4 reserved instances now provisioning; 2 have joined cluster and are warm.
runtime-bot: node-42 rebooted and rejoined as Ready; driver rollback completed; GPUs visible 8/8.
maya (oncall): queue down to ~1.1k and dropping. p99 still elevated but trending down. any customer escalations beyond earlier?
customer-success: one Dedicated enterprise saw transient 5xx spikes but no lasting degradation; they asked for a postmortem.
eli-ml: post-incident recs: require canary window 1h at 10% fleet for driver rollouts; add synthetic memory-pressure tests for new driver versions.
lia-sre: follow-up action items I'll own:
- RCA: driver kernel module regression causing XID/OOM on certain workloads
- tactical: autoscaler circuit-breaker: if XID rate > threshold prefer on-demand and avoid spot/ramp
- infra: increase provider API token bucket and add exponential backoff to autoscaler calls
- dev: block driver rollout until synthetic e2e passes and add golden workloads test
jordan-eng: added runbook PR `docs/runbooks/gpu-autoscale-failures.md` describing steps used here.
maya (oncall): handing off to lia-sre for monitoring. summary pinned. please update INC-2026-0315-09 with timestamps/owners.
lia-sre: monitoring window 2h. owners: lia-sre (incident owner), sam-ops (infra), eli-ml (routing), jordan-eng (autoscaler), customer-success (comms).
customer-success: sending post-incident customer follow-up in 15m. cc @maya
maya (oncall): final notes: peak queue ~9.8k at 14:05Z; autoscaler attempted 7 times; forced instances requested; driver rollback + runtime restarts stabilized nodes by 14:42Z. mitigated but monitoring until queue <200. handing off at 15:00Z. silence alerts 30m to reduce noise while verifying stabilization. :white_check_mark:
